decisions.statement: Use one 24-variable row cube. The logical relation has 14,944,219 rows and a full committed assignment width of 11,437,038 fields for z=x||w. Extend both to the row cube by zero padding.
decisions.reason: The corrected paper permits n_F<=m, a padded identity, and one log(m)-variable SumCheck. Both selected logical widths fit in 2^24.

decisions.statement: Map every logical row and full assignment coordinate to the same zero-based prefix in little-endian Boolean order. Fill all remaining rows with zero and require f_app(0,...,0)=0. Prepend M_0=[I_11437038;0] to the 13 application matrices and lift f to ignore its new first input.
decisions.reason: The injective prefix map and zero constant term are both necessary for logical and padded acceptance equivalence; the padded identity then binds the full assignment norm.

decisions.statement: For b=2 and k=14, use 14 little-endian magnitude bits with one common centered sign per scalar. The prover rejects an out-of-range full assignment, and the verifier rejects an out-of-range public input. The verifier does not inspect private assignment coordinates.
decisions.reason: The paper defines split properties but not one deterministic algorithm.

decisions.statement: Use five complete Phi81 public-input rings. A fresh input has 257 logical fields followed by 13 fixed zeros; a carried input has all 270 authoritative public fields.
decisions.reason: The public input needs one stable, ring-aligned F-prime encoding.

decisions.statement: Use PaddedRowIdentity: the reviewed joint PiCCS polynomial and one SumCheck over the 24-variable row cube, with the padded M_0 identity and the reviewed alpha, gamma, signs, source order, range polynomial, absolute target, and terminal equation.
decisions.reason: This is the corrected paper's zero-row specialization with n_F<=m. It uses the paper's single row-domain SumCheck and adds no authoritative relation field.

decisions.statement: Bind the norm terminal through ct(y_(i,0)) for M_0=[I_11437038;0]. Do not accept a separate NC terminal or optional norm-opening channel.
decisions.reason: The M_0 output is in the CE relation for the same committed assignment, and padded zero rows do not change P_2 acceptance.

decisions.statement: Instantiate the corrected paper strong and weak reductions for the zero-row embedding. Keep phi equal to the commitment projection, use BatchCE_15(B_amb,L) as the shared-point ambient relation, and prove padding refinement before reusing the paper composition theorem.
decisions.reason: The selected profile changes matrix shape but adds no authoritative CE field and no extra challenge family.

decisions.statement: Do not use beta_a, beta_r, beta_m, or any other extra PiCCS batching challenge. PiCCS uses only the reviewed alpha vector, gamma, and SumCheck round challenges.
decisions.reason: One joint polynomial already gives the required batching. Removing unproved coins removes their soundness and transcript obligations.

decisions.statement: Do not add y_carrier, s_col, y_zcol, or a column-opening field to CE authority. Public-carrier evaluations are verifier-derived from x and may be recomputed as an optimization or omitted.
decisions.reason: The public carrier is already authoritative as x. A second carried value adds no binding and creates an unnecessary PiCCS, PiRLC, and PiDEC lifecycle.

decisions.statement: No column projection, constant lift, or replay map exists in PaddedRowIdentity.
decisions.reason: The approved profile removes the column-authority branch.

decisions.statement: Use the selected width-8 Goldilocks Poseidon2 permutation only in proof, transcript, verifier-key digest, public-image digest, and recursive digest paths.
decisions.reason: One hash family reduces the proof and audit boundary.

decisions.statement: Use canonical 8-byte little-endian Goldilocks values, K=F_q[U]/(U^2-7) in c0,c1 order, R=F_q[X]/(X^54+X^27+1) in increasing-degree order, fixed typed container sections, and fail-closed decoding. Use the canonical sparse Structure stream, reject a constant f_app term, and use the exact ChaCha8 Ajtai setup. Compute the verifier-key digest with the selected field duplex over the typed setup seed, dimensions, and Structure stream.
decisions.reason: These rules define one injective statement, one field transcript, one padding-compatible Structure image, and one reproducible commitment matrix.

decisions.statement: Use nightstream-poseidon2-field-duplex-v1 with additive rate absorption, exact numeric tags, length framing, direction padding, the selected event order, and transcript-derived challenges only. Start a fresh zero-state duplex for each fold, link folds by exact typed child-to-running-claim equality, and treat the final fold transcript digest as a native verifier receipt that is not relation authority or next-fold input. A circuit may omit post-challenge receipt-only hashing when its manifest proves that the omitted steps affect neither acceptance nor the public image.
decisions.reason: Challenge-producing transcript behavior and fold links must agree across verifiers; non-authoritative diagnostic work need not add circuit rows.

decisions.statement: For each of 15 rho ring elements and each of 54 coefficients, try at most three indexed transcript candidates. Accept x<q-1 and map x mod 5 to -2,-1,0,1,2. Reject the proof on exhaustion.
decisions.reason: Because q mod 5=1, this gives exact uniform digits with per-fold exhaustion at most 810/q^3 and one bounded native/circuit algorithm.

decisions.statement: The verifier key owns the structure and profile. CE authority is exactly c, x, r, and y_ring. Recompute caches and digests. Reject undeclared extension fields.
decisions.reason: Every value read by acceptance needs one unambiguous authority owner.

decisions.statement: Target at least 96 classical bits for one v1 proof with at most 64 folds. A release must instantiate every bad-event term and reject any verifier-key profile that misses the target.
decisions.reason: The one-fold algebraic count is only a planning term and cannot be presented as end-to-end security.

decisions.statement: Use the classical random-oracle model, one proof and one session per verifier key, at most 64 folds, and at most 262,144 adaptive oracle queries. This query bound includes the derived maximum 157,313 prescribed tagged squeezes per key. Use uniformly generated Ajtai parameters or an explicit seeded-PRG assumption and an expected-polynomial-time proof-of-knowledge target.
decisions.reason: A concrete reduction needs one feasible adversary interface and a resource census that includes the protocol's own challenge schedule.

decisions.statement: Replace the legacy SplitNc circuit with the PaddedRowIdentity verifier. The selected circuit must implement the same 24-round joint SumCheck, acceptance-relevant transcript, bounded sampler, typed claim layout, PiRLC, PiDEC, and terminal public image.
decisions.reason: Circuit correspondence requires one acceptance predicate on both sides without receipt-only rows.

decisions.statement: Use the versioned Spartan-with-WHIR-profile-manifest-v1 family over the selected current-circuit R1CS. The verifier key owns the concrete backend manifest. Unsupported manifests reject, and release requires one concrete manifest plus the matching on-chain parser and verifier identity.
decisions.reason: The protocol can freeze the terminal interface and backend family before a release-specific backend manifest exists.

decisions.statement: Accept conformance evidence only when its named implementation produced the execution, mutation, trace, and build identity, and an independent checker recomputed the semantic result.
decisions.reason: A hand-authored acceptance bit or self-consistent digest is not implementation evidence.
